sources.bodyExcerpt: Vemuram Jan Ray - Mixdown Magazine READING Vemuram Jan Ray Subscribe X Subscribe to Mixdown Magazine Select State NSW QLD VIC ACT TAS SA WA NT --> Subscribe News Features Reviews Directory Giveaways Videos Magazines Privacy & Policies Advertise Contact Terms & Conditions Guitars Vemuram Jan Ray A RAY OF LIGHT There are four controls (and they’re not labelled on the pedal itself, so you might want to memorize them): Volume and Gain on the top row, and Bass and Treble on the bottom row. There’s a fifth control hidden from view though, and this is where that teeny little screwdriver comes into it. There’s a Saturation trim pot on the top of the pedal – turn it to the left to increase the amount of saturation, or to the right to decrease it. Then there’s the usual input and output jacks, 9v DC power supply jack and a true-bypass on/off switch. The finish is an alluring gold-ish hue; it’s pretty damn beautiful. So here’s the deal with the Vemuram Jan Ray: it’s described as ’The Fender Magic 6 sound’. In other words, it’s inspired by the magic that happens to certain Fender amps when the Volume and Treble are on 6, Middle on 3 and Bass on 2 (6, 6, and 3X2 = 6, geddit?). The pedal is designed to offer a very natural-feeling compression but is mainly aimed at giving you those punchy, clear tones of 60s Blackface Fender amps with a crispness on the top along with warmth and softness in the lows. IF YOU’RE 5-5-5 I’M… The first thing you’ll notice about this pedal is that it’s great for clean tones, and the high end doesn’t get harsh so much as clear and airy, which makes it great for brightening up a dark-sounding guitar. The lows never get too ‘boomy’, and they generally feel supportive rather than overpowering. The midrange feels a little bit scooped at lower gain levels, but as you increase the Gain control you’ll notice an increase in midrange fullness along with a ‘smooshy’, smooth saturation. Great for getting some extra mojo out of an ES- 335 or some fatness out of an otherwise thin-sounding Strat. The Saturation trimmer is a very handy little feature. At the lower end of the spectrum this gives you finer control over the amount of drive because you can really dial in the ‘in-between’ response, or it lets you really crank it for a richer, more distort-y overdrive. CUTTING SIX This is a very classy, sophisticated-sounding overdrive that rewards the player with nuanced technique: if you’re more of a gleeful basher you’ll probably prefer something a bit more ragged around the edges compared to this pedal’s more dignified, refined approach to overdrive. For more information, visit the Guitar Factory website. sources.h1: Vemuram Myriad Fuzz: The Brass Box That Started Life As Half Of Something Bigger
sources.description: Vemuram Myriad Fuzz guide: the germanium-silicon hybrid explained, the bias trimmer decoded, verified players, tone settings and 2026 buying advice.
sources.snippet: Vemuram Myriad Fuzz: Josh Smith's Hybrid Fuzz Beast
sources.bodyExcerpt: Vemuram Myriad Fuzz: Josh Smith's Hybrid Fuzz Beast Skip to content Dirty Guitar Facts. Loud Legends. R ock G uitars S tories P eople F orever Search GuitarGangsters ⌕ Menu Home Guitar Legends Gear Rigs Guitars Amps Pedals & FX Pickups Accessories DIY Builds Custom Builds Electronics & Wiring Finishing & Relics Mods & Upgrades Rock History 70’s Rock 80’s Metal 90’s Grunge & Alternative 2000’s Revival News Culture Videos About Contact In this guide The short version Who Josh Smith is, and why the pedal exists Where the Myriad Fuzz came from Specifications What every control does What it actually sounds like Famous players: what actually holds up Six settings that work How it compares Buying guide Living with one FAQ In this guide The short version Who Josh Smith is, and why the pedal exists Where the Myriad Fuzz came from Specifications What every control does What it actually sounds like Famous players: what actually holds up Six settings that work How it compares Buying guide Living with one FAQ Share this article Home › Gear Rigs › Vemuram Myriad Fuzz: The Brass Box That Started Life As Half Of Something Bigger Gear Rigs Vemuram Myriad Fuzz: The Brass Box That Started Life As Half Of Something Bigger Vemuram Myriad Fuzz guide: the germanium-silicon hybrid explained, the bias trimmer decoded, verified players, tone settings and 2026 buying advice. admin 22 September 2026 22 min read GG-ARTICLE-TOP Almost every fuzz pedal ever built is an argument about one transistor family. Germanium is warm, woolly, temperature-flaky and cleans up like a dream. Silicon is loud, spitty, aggressive and reliable. You pick a side, you buy the pedal, and you spend the next decade quietly wishing it did the other thing on Tuesdays. GG-ARTICLE-AFTER-INTRO The Vemuram Myriad Fuzz refuses to pick. It puts a silicon transistor and a vintage germanium transistor in the same signal path, gives you a knob called Feel to move between their characters, and hides a trimmer inside the enclosure that biases the germanium side to taste. It is hand-built in Tokyo, wrapped in solid brass, and it costs more than most people’s first amplifier. It is also, unusually for a signature pedal, the leftover half of a much stranger machine — and the guitarist whose name is on it has been photographed using it on his own board for years, which is more than can be said for a lot of endorsements. This is the full story: where the circuit came from, what every control actually does, who genuinely plays one, how to dial it in, and whether the brass justifies the invoice. How to Get the Tone ↓ The short version The Myriad Fuzz is a hybrid germanium/silicon fuzz, hand-built by Vemuram in Tokyo in a solid brass enclosure, developed with American blues guitarist and producer Josh Smith. It has four external knobs — Level, Fuzz, Feel and Tone — plus an internal Germanium Bias trimmer. It runs on a 9-volt battery or a standard centre-negative 9 V supply, is true bypass, and draws a startlingly small amount of current. Its selling point is range. At low Fuzz settings with the Feel knob backed off it behaves like a thick, saturated overdrive with enormous output on tap. Wound up, it goes into Big Muff territory without the mid-scoop, and it retains a low end that vintage Fuzz Face circuits simply do not have. It cleans up off the guitar volume knob the way good germanium fuzzes do, but it does it without the volume drop and tonal collapse that usually comes with that trick. As of September 2026 it is a $435-and-up pedal in the United States, with Equipboard tracking an average across merchants of $462 and a spread up to roughly $558. It sits in the top price tier of the fuzz category, and it knows it. Who Josh Smith is, and why the pedal exists The résumé Josh Smith was born in Middletown, Connecticut on 7 October 1979 and raised in Fort Lauderdale, Florida. He picked up a guitar at seven, was playing blues festivals at ten, and was making albums at fou

sources.snippet: Vemuram Myriad Fuzz | AllThePedals
sources.bodyExcerpt: Vemuram Myriad Fuzz | AllThePedals Articles Genealogy Browse Search results for " " Gain / Fuzz / Vemuram Myriad Fuzz Myriad Fuzz The Vemuram Myriad Fuzz, a collaboration with Josh Smith, is a versatile fuzz pedal blending silicon and vintage germanium transistors. Offering a wide tonal range from spitty to smooth overdrive fuzz, it features a trimmer for germanium bias control, allowing for dynamic and organic fuzz tones. Its design is inspired by the best vintage fuzzes. What Vemuram say about the Myriad Fuzz A collaboration pedal with Josh Smith. The Myriad Fuzz is a hybrid between a Silicon transistor and a vintage Germanium transistor. The range of the tone is very wide and has enough head room to control the fuzz tone from spitty fuzz to a smooth overdrive fuzz. The trimmer allows you to control the Germanium Bias with the FEEL knob which will affect the tone of the fuzz. Josh Smith's Comment "The Myriad fuzz started life as one half of my larger Myriad pedal. When it started to become clear how great the fuzz sounded we knew it would need to be released on its own. This is the fuzz I've had in my mind for over 10 years. A unique fuzz that employ's both Germanium and Silicon transistors. It is incredibly tweak-able but never complicated. There is no bad sounds in this pedal. No matter where you set the knobs you get great tone. It goes from fire breathing silicon to cool warm germanium easily, it cleans up like the best vintage fuzzes, adn is more dynamic and organic than any fuzz has the right to be. Myriad took more than 2 years to complete with Josh Smith’s inspirational idea. This pedal is a mixture of the Myriad Fuzz, Loop, and a mixer that can do literally “Myriad” of combinations. The fuzz can be switched between 2 outputs and lets you mix the loop and the fuzz if the signal is in the wet chain. (Please see the attached matrix table inside the control manual for more details) The Mix can be controlled by an expression pedal or the control knob on the center of the pedal (red knob). A unique fuzz that employ's both Germanium and Silicon transistors. It goes from fire breathing silicon to cool warm germanium easily, it cleans up just like the vintage fuzzes, and is more dynamic and organic. It goes from a spitty to smooth driven sound. It also has a large amount of volume on tap and a tone circuit that allows it to really work live. The Myriad can plug into 2 amps to let you achieve countless options with other effects, a new generation concept with Myriad of combinations. “The Myriad is the end result of years of ideas and exploration. I wanted a way to be creative in a two amp situation, this pedal cracks the code on creativity by giving you literally “myriad” of routing options and possibilities. Plus, in my opinion the best fuzz pedal in the world." sources.bodyExcerpt: Vemuram Myriad Fuzz: Josh Smith's Hybrid Fuzz Beast Skip to content Dirty Guitar Facts. Loud Legends. R ock G uitars S tories P eople F orever Search GuitarGangsters ⌕ Menu Home Guitar Legends Gear Rigs Guitars Amps Pedals & FX Pickups Accessories DIY Builds Custom Builds Electronics & Wiring Finishing & Relics Mods & Upgrades Rock History 70’s Rock 80’s Metal 90’s Grunge & Alternative 2000’s Revival News Culture Videos About Contact In this guide The short version Who Josh Smith is, and why the pedal exists Where the Myriad Fuzz came from Specifications What every control does What it actually sounds like Famous players: what actually holds up Six settings that work How it compares Buying guide Living with one FAQ In this guide The short version Who Josh Smith is, and why the pedal exists Where the Myriad Fuzz came from Specifications What every control does What it actually sounds like Famous players: what actually holds up Six settings that work How it compares Buying guide Living with one FAQ Share this article Home › Gear Rigs › Vemuram Myriad Fuzz: The Brass Box That Started Life As Half Of Something Bigger Gear Rigs Vemuram Myriad Fuzz: The Brass Box That Started Life As Half Of Something Bigger Vemuram Myriad Fuzz guide: the germanium-silicon hybrid explained, the bias trimmer decoded, verified players, tone settings and 2026 buying advice. admin 22 September 2026 22 min read GG-ARTICLE-TOP Almost every fuzz pedal ever built is an argument about one transistor family. Germanium is warm, woolly, temperature-flaky and cleans up like a dream. Silicon is loud, spitty, aggressive and reliable. You pick a side, you buy the pedal, and you spend the next decade quietly wishing it did the other thing on Tuesdays. GG-ARTICLE-AFTER-INTRO The Vemuram Myriad Fuzz refuses to pick. It puts a silicon transistor and a vintage germanium transistor in the same signal path, gives you a knob called Feel to move between their characters, and hides a trimmer inside the enclosure that biases the germanium side to taste. It is hand-built in Tokyo, wrapped in solid brass, and it costs more than most people’s first amplifier. It is also, unusually for a signature pedal, the leftover half of a much stranger machine — and the guitarist whose name is on it has been photographed using it on his own board for years, which is more than can be said for a lot of endorsements. This is the full story: where the circuit came from, what every control actually does, who genuinely plays one, how to dial it in, and whether the brass justifies the invoice. How to Get the Tone ↓ The short version The Myriad Fuzz is a hybrid germanium/silicon fuzz, hand-built by Vemuram in Tokyo in a solid brass enclosure, developed with American blues guitarist and producer Josh Smith. It has four external knobs — Level, Fuzz, Feel and Tone — plus an internal Germanium Bias trimmer. It runs on a 9-volt battery or a standard centre-negative 9 V supply, is true bypass, and draws a startlingly small amount of current. Its selling point is range. At low Fuzz settings with the Feel knob backed off it behaves like a thick, saturated overdrive with enormous output on tap. Wound up, it goes into Big Muff territory without the mid-scoop, and it retains a low end that vintage Fuzz Face circuits simply do not have. It cleans up off the guitar volume knob the way good germanium fuzzes do, but it does it without the volume drop and tonal collapse that usually comes with that trick. As of September 2026 it is a $435-and-up pedal in the United States, with Equipboard tracking an average across merchants of $462 and a spread up to roughly $558. It sits in the top price tier of the fuzz category, and it knows it. Who Josh Smith is, and why the pedal exists The résumé Josh Smith was born in Middletown, Connecticut on 7 October 1979 and raised in Fort Lauderdale, Florida. He picked up a guitar at seven, was playing blues festivals at ten, and was making albums at fou

The Shanks 4K was designed to recreate the classic 60s Fuzz Face overdrive/boost sound using vintage germanium transistors. The 4K designation refers to its four knobs: Level, Fuzz, Bass, and Treble, offering more tonal control than vintage two-knob designs. Two vintage germanium transistors deliver authentic Fuzz Face character, while a modern output circuit provides higher headroom than original designs. The Fuzz Color trim potentiometer on the front of the solid brass housing allows precise adjustment of the distortion character. The tonal range is exceptionally wide, from firm and bright clean tones to edgy, crunchy boost and full-on vintage fuzz. Controls include Level, Fuzz, Bass, and Treble, plus the front-mounted Fuzz Color trimmer. IMPORTANT: Do not use higher voltage than 9V with this pedal - it is specifically created and designed for 9V operation only. The germanium circuit provides touch-sensitive response that cleans up beautifully with your guitar's volume knob. sources.bodyExcerpt: Vemuram Shanks 4K: - Supernice!エフェクター ランキング 特集記事 カテゴリから探す メーカーから探す ランキング エフェクター ファズ Vemuram Shanks 4K Vemuram Shanks 4K メーカー VEMURAM カテゴリ ファズ 発売時期 2014年 価格 41,000 円 (税込) コンテンツの誤りを送信する Amazon で購入する 楽天市場 で購入する Yahoo! で購入する 石橋楽器 で購入する Shanks 4K は、アメリカの音楽プロデューサー／ギタリストである John Shanks と VEMRUM のコラボレーションによって誕生した、ゲルマニウムトランジスタを使用したファズ・ペダル。旧モデル「Shanks 3K」からノブを一つ増やした4ノブ仕様で、3K よりもゲインが高めに設定されたモデルです。 2つのゲルマニウムトランジスター、厳選したヴィンテージ N.O.S コンデンサーを採用するなど、ビンテージなサウンド設計に最新パーツを使用し、ノイズレスでヘッドルームの大きいファズサウンドを実現しています。 ボディ上部の Fuzz Colorトリマーの操作によって、プチプチ系ファズからスムーズなドライブ感までを微調整ができます。 60年代後半の Fazz Face を元に開発され、シングルコイルとの相性も良好でハムバッカー・ギターでも芯が残ったコシのある音作りが可能。タッチは非常に敏感で、繊細に弾けば煌びやかなクリーン／エッジの効いたクランチ／巻弦が跳ねる分厚いディストーションと、ピッキングの強弱やギターのボリューム・コントロール、4つのノブの設定によって幅広い音作りが可能。ツマミの調節でクリーンブースターとしても使うことができます。 仕様 ■コントロール：Bass, Treble, Volume, Fuzz, トリマー（Fuzz Color、Bias） ■電源：9V電池、9VDCアダプター ■寸法：70（W）×112（D）×51（H）mm ■重量：425g ※当サイトではアフィリエイトプログラムを利用して商品を紹介しています。 Amazon 楽天 Yahoo!
